Agarican, Psibyl CR 15

XP 51,200
LN Medium plant (fungus)
Init +9; Senses low-light vision, thoughtsense 60 ft.; Perception +31

DEFENSE

AC 31, touch 15, flat-footed 26 (+4 Dex, +1 dodge, +16 natural)
hp 209 (22d8+110)
Fort +18, Ref +13, Will +13; Immune plant traits; Resist fire 10, electricity 10

OFFENSE

Speed fly 30 ft. (perfect)
Melee 10 tentacles +18 (1d6+2 plus poison)
Psychic Magic (CL 15th; concentration +21)

27 PE—ectoplasmic snare (3 PE, DC 18), ghost whip (2 PE), hypercognition (2 PE), mindlink (1 PE), mind probe (4 PE, DC 19), telekinetic storm (9 PE, DC 24), withdraw affliction (6 PE)

Spell-like Abilities (CL 15th; concentration +21)

Constant—speak with plants, greensight
At will—burst of nettles (DC 18), dust of twilight (DC 17), entangle (DC 16), fungal infestation (DC 18), pernicious poison (DC 17), spore burst (DC 18), telekinesis (DC 20)
3/day—control plants (DC 24), prismatic glow (DC 21), vine strike (DC 18)

STATISTICS

Str 15, Dex 20, Con 20, Int 21, Wis 19, Cha 14
Base Atk +16; CMB +18, CMD 34
Feats Combat Casting, Combat Expertise, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Iron Will, Improved Initiative, Lunge, Mobility, Spell Focus (Enchantment), Spring Attack, Verdant Spell
Skills Bluff +24, Intimidate +24, Knowledge (dungeoneering, geography, nature) +27, Perception +31, Sense Motive +28
Languages Agaric, Aklo, Common, Sylvan, Terran, Undercommon; telepathy 100 ft.
SQ compression

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Luminescent Lamella (Ex)

The glowing markings and tendrils of a psibyl constantly emit a soft light, equivalent to that of a candle. This light brightens to the equivalent of a torch when they are using any of their spell-like abilities or psychic magic, or the sending or witness functions of their psychic spores ability.

Poison (Ex)

Tentacle—injury; save Fort DC 21; frequency 1/round for 4 rounds; effect 1d3 Wis & 1 Int; cure 1 save. Save DC is Con-based.

Psychic Spores (Su)

A creature coming within 30 feet of a psibyl must make a DC 23 Fortitude save every round they remain within range or be infected by an inhaled form of their spores. A psibyl can sense the direction of any creature infected with their psychic spores, and if the creature is within 1 mile they can sense its precise location. As a standard action, a psibyl may cast sending, targeting any creature it has infected with its psychic spores, though the infected creature may choose to make a new saving throw against the psychic spores instead of responding to the sending.

A psibyl may choose to briefly channel the full weight of their minds into the psychic connection granted by the spores, allowing them to cast witness (Will DC 19) with no limit on range on a target afflicted by their spores. The spores burn out upon the conclusion of the spell or the success of the saving throw against it and no longer infect the character.

Psychic spores can’t be removed by spells that heal hit point damage, such as cure spells, but can be affected by spells capable of neutralizing poison, such as neutralize poison or heal. Immunity to poison also grants immunity from this effect, although agaricians generally allow themselves to be infected despite their immunity.

ABOUT

Environment temperate forests or swamps
Organization solitary or bloom (1 psibyl plus 6-12 amanites, 2-6 aserubra, 15-45 bolites, 30-90 hoplites, and 2-8 toxiphages)
Treasure double

Psibyls are the leaders of the agaricians, the psychic masterminds who coordinate life within the great fungal blooms. Their powerful mental abilities allow them to command and organize their less intelligent brethren from afar, and it is fair to say that agarician society could not function in their absence.

In appearance, psibyls are among the most slender of all agaricians. Their earth-toned fungal flesh has a light crystalline dust across it. Veins of bioluminescent blues and indigos curl down from under the brim of their cowl-like mushroom caps, swirling over their ‘faces’ in unique symmetrical patterns that are eerily reminiscent of facial features.

Their forms, though easy to mistake for humanoid, look less familiar the more one watches them—the sheets of fungus that hang from their frames, looking nearly like a robe when still, separate and shuffle when it moves, revealing the countless entwined stalks that make up the creature’s body. Though easy to mistake for shoulders, the widening beneath the neck is the branching of the creature’s body, and any adherence it may show to a humanoid form is a choice. The glowing veins on its face seem to branch into solidly glowing tendrils that weave through their form. While using certain whip-like spells, these glowing tendrils seem to extend and blend into the spell itself.

A secret unknown to all but the sibyls themselves is how they are created—the truth is that they can only be created directly by an existing sibyl investing a portion of its power into an exemplary bolite, the most mutable of all agaricians. The resulting new sibyl will soon feel drawn to leave the bloom and seek out a suitable spot for a new one. How they determine the spot is unknown, as is how they seed the characteristic giant shelf mushrooms, but given a few months and good fortune, new lights will begin to glow under mouldering branches.
